reason: The text demonstrates multiple instances of Hebrew people actively expressing their views. King Ahab, King Jehoshaphat, the 400 prophets, and Micaiah all articulate different perspectives. While the narrative shows social pressure on Micaiah to conform to the other prophets' message (the official attempts to persuade him: 'הִנֵּה־ נָ֞א דִּבְרֵ֧י הַנְּבִיאִ֛ים'), Micaiah explicitly refuses to be silenced, declaring 'חַי־ יְהוָ֕ה כִּ֠י אֶת־ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יֹאמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֵלַ֖י אֹת֥וֹ אֲדַבֵּֽר' (As the Lord lives, what the Lord says to me, that I will speak). He proceeds to deliver his true prophecy despite opposition and even physical assault. The text shows discouragement of conformity rather than successful suppression of expression.
